2	
3	**Purpose (descriptive only).** Find out whether the local git history of the ordinary working clone contains WP-4C-1 execution work, and find the earliest reproducible trace that the system recorded. This protocol **captures evidence only**. It does not judge whether any work conformed to any norm, and it contains no hypothesis, falsifier or score.
4	
5	## 1. Target
6	**Normalisation (before any test).** Each Unicode hyphen or dash is replaced by an ASCII `-`. The replaced characters are U+2010, U+2011, U+2012, U+2013, U+2014, U+2015, U+2212, U+FE58, U+FE63, U+FF0D and U+00AD (soft hyphen). The text is padded with one space on each side. Tests run byte-wise under `LC_ALL=C`.
7	
8	| Rule | Matches (case-insensitive letters) | Left boundary | Right boundary |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| **T1** | `WP-4C-1` | previous char not `[0-9A-Za-z]` | next char not `[0-9A-Za-z]`, **and** the next two chars are not `-<digit>` or `.<digit>` |
11	| **T2** (alias) | `wp4c1-` | previous char not `[0-9A-Za-z]` | none (the hyphen is the boundary) |
12	
13	`_`, `/`, `.`, spaces and punctuation count as boundaries. So `WP-4C-1.`, `(WP-4C-1)`, `x_wp4c1-evidence.md` and `WP-4C-1-acceptance` all match.
14	
15	**Excluded near-matches:**
16	- `WP-4C-2`, `WP-4B`, `WP-4D`: these are sibling items, not the target.
17	- `WP-4C` with no `-1` after it: this is the parent item. It names a scope, not this item.
18	- `WP-4C-10`, `WP-4C-1a`: the identifier continues with an alphanumeric character, so it names a different item.
19	- `WP-4C-1.2`, `WP-4C-1-2`: these read as a sub-item or a range. They are a longer identifier, so the protocol does not treat them as WP-4C-1.
20	- `xWP-4C-1`, `swp4c1-`: there is no left boundary.
21	- Unattested spellings (`WP4C1`, `WP-4C1`, `wp_4c_1`, `wp4c1_`, `WP 4C 1`): neither the register nor the facts give these spellings. Matching them would add false positives without any stated basis.
22	
23	**Where the protocol looks.** It searches every commit reachable from the captured refs, with no date or ancestry filter, in four places:
24	- `message`: the full raw message (`%B`).
25	- `trailer`: the parsed trailers (`%(trailers:only,unfold)`). A trailer hit is also a `message` hit.
26	- `path`: changed file paths (`--name-only`).
27	- `added_line`: added diff lines only (`-p -U0`; lines starting with `+`).
28	
29	Renames are not detected (`--no-renames`), and external diff and textconv are off. A **merge's own changes** come from the combined diff (`--diff-merges=combined`): only paths that differ from *every* parent, and only lines added relative to *every* parent (all `+` columns). The side branch's changes are therefore never attributed to the merge. Side-branch commits are scanned separately, as ordinary commits.
30	
31	## 2. Path classes and commit classification
32	Each changed path is lower-cased. The first rule that matches assigns its class:
33	- **P-DOC (documentation / governance):**
34	  - a directory segment is one of `doc docs governance ruling rulings decision decisions adr adrs plan plans planning evidence minutes notes report reports register registers`; or
35	  - the extension is one of `.md .markdown .rst .txt .adoc .org .pdf .doc .docx .odt`; or
36	  - the basename starts with `register|registers|ruling|rulings|decision|decisions|plan|plans|acceptance|adr`, followed by `-`, `_`, `.` or the end of the name.
37	- **P-TEST:**
38	  - a directory segment is one of `test tests __tests__ spec specs e2e`; or
39	  - the basename matches `^test_`, `[._]test\.`, `[._]spec\.` or `^conftest\.py$`.
40	- **P-CODE:**
41	  - the extension is one of `sh bash py js mjs cjs ts tsx jsx go rs java kt rb php c h cc cpp hpp cs swift scala sql lua pl r ps1`; or
42	  - the basename is `makefile`, `dockerfile` or `justfile`.

44	
45	"Code/test path" means P-TEST ∪ P-CODE. P-DOC takes precedence, so `docs/x.py` is P-DOC.
46

50	|---|---|---|
51	| C1 | ≥ 2 parents | **MERGE** |
52	| C2 | K ≠ ∅ and (*msg* or *kref*) | **EXECUTION-TRACE** |
53	| C3 | ≥ 1 changed path and all changed paths are P-DOC | **DOC-OR-GOVERNANCE** |

56

66	- **Fixed statement:** "completeness vs the host NOT shown".

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# capture_a.sh -- Protocol A (PROTOCOL-A.md): capture evidence of WP-4C-1 in the local git history.
3	# Captures evidence only: no norm check, hypothesis, falsifier or score. Read-only: git log/for-each-ref/rev-list
4	# (plus `git --version`).
5	# Usage: bash /path/to/capture_a.sh OUTDIR   (from the repository root or any subdirectory of the working clone;
6	#        OUTDIR must be absent or empty, and should lie outside the repository)
7	# Exit: 0 complete | 1 complete with unexpected exit codes (00_errors.tsv; absence then NOT asserted) | 2 refused to start
8	set -u -o pipefail
9	# Resolve our own absolute path FIRST, before any cd (r2 self-hash defect).
10	SELF="$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'capture_a: cannot resolve own path\n' >&2; exit 2; }
11	export LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC GIT_PAGER=cat PAGER=cat GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
12	  GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1
13	unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES GIT_NAMESPACE
14	TAB=$'\t'
15	die() { printf 'capture_a: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 2; }
16	[ "$#" -eq 1 ] && [ -n "$1" ] || die "usage: capture_a.sh OUTDIR"
17	OUT="$(realpath -m -- "$1")" || die "cannot resolve OUTDIR"
18	if [ -e "$OUT" ]; then { [ -d "$OUT" ] && [ -z "$(ls -A -- "$OUT")" ]; } || die "OUTDIR exists and is not empty"; fi
19	git --no-pager for-each-ref --count=1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "not inside a git repository"
20	mkdir -p -- "$OUT" || die "cannot create OUTDIR"
21	ERR="$OUT/00_errors.tsv"; : > "$ERR"; : > "$OUT/00_stderr.log"
22	ok() { # ok LABEL RC ALLOWED... : record an unexpected exit code; never aborts
23	  local l="$1" rc="$2" a; shift 2
24	  for a in "$@"; do [ "$rc" -eq "$a" ] && return 0; done
25	  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$l" "$rc" >> "$ERR"; return 1
26	}
27	g() { git --no-pager -c core.quotepath=false -c diff.noprefix=false -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false -c diff.relative=false \
28	  -c diff.renames=false -c log.showRoot=true -c log.showSignature=false -c color.ui=never "$@" 2>>"$OUT/00_stderr.log"; }
29	D=(--no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames --no-relative --diff-merges=combined)
30	finish() { # remove temporaries, hash every output, exit
31	  rm -f -- "$OUT"/.tmp_*
32	  ( cd -- "$OUT" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS -print | sort | xargs -r -d '\n' sha256sum ) > "$OUT/SHA256SUMS" \
33	    || { printf 'capture_a: hashing failed\n' >&2; exit 1; }
34	  exit "$1"
35	}
36	
37	# ---- awk prelude: hyphen normalisation, match rules T1/T2 (section 1), path classes (section 2) ----
38	FN='BEGIN { FS = "\t"; US = "\036"
39	  HY = "\342\200\220|\342\200\221|\342\200\222|\342\200\223|\342\200\224|\342\200\225|\342\210\222|\357\271\230|\357\271\243|\357\274\215|\302\255" }
40	function hit(s,   t, u, nx, r) {
41	  t = " " s " "; gsub(HY, "-", t); u = t; r = ""
42	  while (match(u, /[^0-9A-Za-z][Ww][Pp]-4[Cc]-1/)) {
43	    nx = substr(u, RSTART + RLENGTH, 2)
44	    if (nx !~ /^[0-9A-Za-z]/ && nx !~ /^[-.][0-9]/) { r = "T1"; break }
45	    u = substr(u, RSTART + 1) }
46	  if (t ~ /[^0-9A-Za-z][Ww][Pp]4[Cc]1-/) r = (r == "") ? "T2" : r "+T2"
47	  return r }
48	function pclass(p,   q, b) {
49	  q = "/" tolower(p); b = q; sub(/.*\//, "", b)
50	  if (q ~ /\/(docs?|governance|rulings?|decisions?|adrs?|plans?|planning|evidence|minutes|notes|reports?|registers?)\//) return "DOC"
51	  if (b ~ /\.(md|markdown|rst|txt|adoc|org|pdf|docx?|odt)$/) return "DOC"
52	  if (b ~ /^(registers?|rulings?|decisions?|plans?|acceptance|adr)([-_.]|$)/) return "DOC"
53	  if (q ~ /\/(tests?|__tests__|specs?|e2e)\// || b ~ /^test_|[._]test\.|[._]spec\.|^conftest\.py$/) return "TEST"
54	  if (b ~ /\.(sh|bash|py|js|mjs|cjs|ts|tsx|jsx|go|rs|java|kt|rb|php|c|h|cc|cpp|hpp|cs|swift|scala|sql|lua|pl|r|ps1)$/) return "CODE"
55	  if (b ~ /^(makefile|dockerfile|justfile)$/) return "CODE"
56	  return "OTHER" }
57	'
58	
59	# ---- meta (no paths, no names) ----
60	SS="$(sha256sum < "$SELF")"; ok self.sha256 $? 0
61	{ printf 'protocol\tA\nscript_sha256\t%s\ngit_version\t%s\n' "${SS%% *}" "$(git --version)"
62	  printf 'capture\tLOCAL_REF_SET\ncompleteness_vs_host\tNOT SHOWN\n'; } > "$OUT/00_meta.tsv"
63

# PROTOCOL A — evidence capture for WP-4C-1 (fixed in advance; implemented by `capture_a.sh`) — r1

**Purpose (descriptive only).** Find out whether the local git history of the ordinary working clone contains WP-4C-1 execution work, and find the earliest reproducible trace that the system recorded. This protocol **captures evidence only**. It does not judge whether any work conformed to any norm, and it contains no hypothesis, falsifier or score.

## 1. Target
**Normalisation (before any test).** Each Unicode hyphen or dash is replaced by an ASCII `-`. The replaced characters are U+2010, U+2011, U+2012, U+2013, U+2014, U+2015, U+2212, U+FE58, U+FE63, U+FF0D and U+00AD (soft hyphen). The text is padded with one space on each side. Tests run byte-wise under `LC_ALL=C`.

| Rule | Matches (case-insensitive letters) | Left boundary | Right boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | `WP-4C-1` | previous char not `[0-9A-Za-z]` | next char not `[0-9A-Za-z]`, **and** the next two chars are not `-<digit>` or `.<digit>` |
| **T2** (alias) | `wp4c1-` | previous char not `[0-9A-Za-z]` | none (the hyphen is the boundary) |

`_`, `/`, `.`, spaces and punctuation count as boundaries. So `WP-4C-1.`, `(WP-4C-1)`, `x_wp4c1-evidence.md` and `WP-4C-1-acceptance` all match.

**Excluded near-matches:**
- `WP-4C-2`, `WP-4B`, `WP-4D`: these are sibling items, not the target.
- `WP-4C` with no `-1` after it: this is the parent item. It names a scope, not this item.
- `WP-4C-10`, `WP-4C-1a`: the identifier continues with an alphanumeric character, so it names a different item.
- `WP-4C-1.2`, `WP-4C-1-2`: these read as a sub-item or a range. They are a longer identifier, so the protocol does not treat them as WP-4C-1.
- `xWP-4C-1`, `swp4c1-`: there is no left boundary.
- Unattested spellings (`WP4C1`, `WP-4C1`, `wp_4c_1`, `wp4c1_`, `WP 4C 1`): neither the register nor the facts give these spellings. Matching them would add false positives without any stated basis.

**Where the protocol looks.** It searches every commit reachable from the captured refs, with no date or ancestry filter, in four places:
- `message`: the full raw message (`%B`).
- `trailer`: the parsed trailers (`%(trailers:only,unfold)`). A trailer hit is also a `message` hit.
- `path`: changed file paths (`--name-only`).
- `added_line`: added diff lines only (`-p -U0`; lines starting with `+`). The path of an added line is taken from the `+++ b/…` header. Git appends a TAB to that header when the path contains a space; **the trailing TAB is stripped before the path is classified** (r1, N3).

Renames are not detected (`--no-renames`), and external diff and textconv are off. A **merge's own changes** come from the combined diff (`--diff-merges=combined`): only paths that differ from *every* parent, and only lines added relative to *every* parent (all `+` columns). The side branch's changes are therefore never attributed to the merge. Side-branch commits are scanned separately, as ordinary commits.

## 2. Path classes and commit classification
Each changed path (repository-relative, as git prints it) is lower-cased. Its **root** is the text before the first `/`; a top-level file (no `/`) has no root.

**Precedence: ROOT first, THEN extension.** The root alone decides which step applies; the extension is consulted only inside that step. No directory-segment word and no basename word (plan, register, report, decision, acceptance, evidence, notes, …) is consulted anywhere, so a generic word can never override a CODE or TEST root (B2). The first step whose root matches assigns the class:

| Step | Root | Class |
|---|---|---|
